Canada's defence policy, Our North, Strong and Free: A Renewed Vision for Canada's Defence [C4, C6, C7], describes AI-enabled modernization as central to the digitalization of defence [C4], which is key to embracing innovation and experimentation and adopting emerging technologies. [C4] The Canadian Armed Forces is updating its tools and processes to better suit them to the modern world. [C4] It will make full use of digital technologies by overhauling outdated and analog processes to improve its ability to hire people, conduct security screening, and share information in a timely way. [C4] This includes expanding the use of artificial intelligence-driven data management tools, as well as initiatives to advance big data management, acquire analytical tools, and expand cloud-based computing on open and secure networks. [C4] These digital initiatives will build a data-driven organization capable of transforming data into actionable information that will allow for rapid decision-making and near real-time responses. [C4] It will also ensure the Canadian Armed Forces can remain interoperable with Canada's most important allies and partners well into the future. [C4]

The DND/CAF AI Strategy describes AI-enabled modernization as foundational to defence modernization. [C3] The fusion of AI, networking, predictive and prescriptive analytics, ML, and robotics will be critical to equip DND/CAF and digitally transform defence. [C3] This will provide the capabilities needed to ensure operational superiority over adversaries and technological parity and interoperability with allies. [C3] AI-enabled capabilities can allow DND/CAF to improve the accuracy of its intelligence, targeting, situational awareness, and decision making, while enabling logistic and corporate efficiencies and improving services. [C8] To achieve these gains, however, DND/CAF must put in place the necessary environments, data management practices and guardrails to ensure that AI is safe, ethical, inclusive, legal, and trusted. [C8] DND/CAF must manage change so as to support innovation, and ensure that its personnel, both now and in the future, have the training and skills that they need to implement AI initiatives successfully. [C8] DND/CAF must also forge partnerships outside the organization to take advantage of promising innovations, and to ensure that its AI-enabled capabilities complement and interoperate with those of its defence partners. [C8]

Strongest source pages: 3 [C4], 2 [C3], 7. [C8]
